title: Wishes and requests: quiero que vengas
summary: Want, hope, ask, advise, allow or forbid someone else to do something with que + subjunctive; keep the infinitive when it's the same person.
focus: Infinitive vs. que + present subjunctive after verbs of wishing and influence; decir que; ojalá and set wishes
content:
## Same person or someone else?

With **querer**, **esperar**, **preferir** and **necesitar**, ask who does the second action. Same person: the **infinitive**. Someone else: **que + subjunctive**.

| verb | same person | someone else |
|---|---|---|
| querer | **Quiero ir.** (I want to go.) | **Quiero que vayas.** (I want you to go.) |
| esperar | **Espero llegar pronto.** | **Espero que llegues pronto.** |
| preferir | **Prefiero cocinar yo.** | **Prefiero que cocines tú.** |
| necesitar | **Necesito descansar.** | **Necesito que me ayudes.** |

English says *I want you to go*; Spanish says *I want that you go*: **quiero que vayas**. Never *quiero que ir*, and never *quiero que vaya* when you are the one going.

## Asking, advising, allowing, forbidding

Verbs that push someone else to act take **que + subjunctive**: **pedir** (to ask), **recomendar**, **aconsejar** (to advise), **permitir** (to allow) and **prohibir** (to forbid), usually with an indirect pronoun for the person.

- **Te pido que me esperes.** I'm asking you to wait for me.
- **Le recomiendo que pruebe el pescado.** I recommend you try the fish. (usted)
- **Os aconsejo que salgáis temprano.** I advise you to leave early.
- **Mi jefe no permite que comamos en la oficina.** My boss doesn't let us eat in the office.
- **Nos prohíben que aparquemos aquí.** They forbid us to park here.

**Permitir** and **prohibir** may also take a plain infinitive: **te prohíbo salir**. Watch the accent: **prohíbo, prohíbe**.

## Decir: telling or reporting

**Decir** has two jobs, and the mood shows which one:

| sentence | meaning | mood |
|---|---|---|
| **Dice que viene.** | She says she's coming. (a report) | indicative |
| **Me dice que venga.** | She tells me to come. (an order) | subjunctive |

- **Ana dice que tiene hambre.** Ana says she's hungry.
- **Ana nos dice que comamos ya.** Ana tells us to eat now.

After a past verb (*me dijo que viniera*) Spanish uses the imperfect subjunctive, which you meet at B2.

## Ojalá and good wishes

**Ojalá** (*I hope*, *let's hope*) always takes the subjunctive, with or without **que**: **Ojalá (que) llueva.** Let's hope it rains.

A bare **que** + subjunctive makes a ready-made wish (an unspoken *espero* in front):

- **¡Que te mejores!** Get well soon!
- **¡Que aproveche!** Enjoy your meal!
- **¡Que tengas suerte!** Good luck!
- **¡Que lo pases bien!** Have a good time!

The verb follows the person: **¡Que se mejore!** (usted), **¡Que lo paséis bien!** (vosotros).

vocabulary.example: Quiero que vengas a mi cumpleaños.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I want you to come to my birthday party.

vocabulary.example: Espero que te guste el regalo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hope you like the present.

vocabulary.example: Necesito que me prestes tu coche.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I need you to lend me your car.

vocabulary.example: Le pido al camarero que nos traiga la cuenta.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I ask the waiter to bring us the bill.
I recommend that you visit Toledo.

vocabulary.example: Mi profesora me aconseja que lea en español.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My teacher advises me to read in Spanish.

vocabulary.example: El dueño prohíbe que fumemos en el piso.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The owner forbids us to smoke in the flat.

vocabulary.example: Mis padres no permiten que mi hermano use el móvil en la mesa.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My parents don't let my brother use his phone at the table.

vocabulary.meaning: to say that (+ indicative) / to tell (someone) to (+ subjunctive)
vocabulary.example: Mi madre me dice que vuelva pronto.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My mother tells me to come back early.
I hope we pass the exam.
You've got the flu? Get well soon!
I see you're eating. Enjoy your meal!

vocabulary.example: Mañana tienes la entrevista, ¿no? ¡Que tengas suerte!
vocabulary.example_meaning: Your interview is tomorrow, isn't it? Good luck!

quiz.prompt: Esta noche estoy cansada. Prefiero ___ en casa.
quiz.explanation: The same person prefers and stays, so the infinitive: prefiero quedarme. 'Que me quede' is only for someone else.
hints: Who prefers? Who stays? The same person?

quiz.prompt: Mis padres quieren que yo ___ medicina.
quiz.explanation: The parents want, I study: two different people, so que + subjunctive: estudie.
hints: Different subjects after querer take que + subjunctive.
-ar verbs swap to -e in the subjunctive.

quiz.prompt: Espero que ___ (tú, tener) un buen viaje.
quiz.explanation: Esperar que + a different subject takes the subjunctive. Tengo becomes tenga, then tengas.
hints: Start from the yo form: tengo.

quiz.prompt: El médico me recomienda que ___ (beber) más agua.
quiz.explanation: Recomendar que pushes someone else to act: subjunctive. Bebo becomes beba.
hints: -er verbs swap to -a in the subjunctive.
Who drinks? Me, the patient: yo.

quiz.prompt: Te pido que no ___ (llegar, tú) tarde mañana.
quiz.explanation: Pedir que + subjunctive. Llegar keeps its hard g sound with gu: llegue, llegues.
hints: Spelling: g becomes gu before e.

quiz.prompt: Ana dice que ___ muy cansada. (She is reporting how she feels.)
quiz.explanation: Decir que reports a fact here, so the indicative: Ana dice que está cansada.

quiz.prompt: Mi madre me dice que ___ mi habitación. (She tells me to tidy it.)
quiz.explanation: Decir que as an order (tell someone to) takes the subjunctive: ordene.
hints: An order with decir takes the subjunctive.

quiz.explanation: Ojalá always takes the subjunctive. Hago becomes haga.
hints: Start from the yo form: hago.

quiz.prompt: Your friend has a bad cold. What do you say?
quiz.explanation: ¡Que te mejores! wishes someone a quick recovery. ¡Que aproveche! is for a meal, ¡Que lo pases bien! for a party or trip, ¡Que tengas suerte! for an exam or interview.

conversations.title: A favour for the weekend
conversations.scenario: Clara is going away for the weekend and asks her flatmate Diego to look after the flat and the cat.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Diego, este fin de semana me voy a Sevilla. ¿Puedo pedirte un favor?
lines.meaning: Diego, I'm off to Seville this weekend. Can I ask you a favour?

lines.speaker: b
lines.meaning: Of course. What do you need?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Necesito que riegues mis plantas el sábado.
lines.meaning: I need you to water my plants on Saturday.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Sí. Te pido que no abras la ventana del salón.
lines.meaning: Yes. Please don't open the living-room window.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Tranquila. ¿Prefieres que te mande fotos del gato?
lines.meaning: Don't worry. Would you like me to send you photos of the cat?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¡Sí, por favor! Ojalá no se aburra sin mí.
lines.meaning: Yes, please! I hope he doesn't get bored without me.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Mi madre dice que los gatos no echan de menos a nadie.
lines.meaning: My mother says cats don't miss anybody.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¡Qué malo eres! Bueno, me voy ya.
lines.meaning: You're so mean! Right, I'm off.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¡Que tengas buen viaje y que lo pases muy bien!
lines.meaning: Have a good trip and have a great time!

listening.meaning: I want you to listen to me.
I need you to help me today.

listening.text: Ojalá no llueva este fin de semana.
listening.meaning: I hope it doesn't rain this weekend.

listening.text: Mi jefa prefiere que trabajemos desde casa.
listening.meaning: My boss prefers us to work from home.
listening.note: New word: la jefa = the boss.

listening.text: Te recomiendo que pruebes el gazpacho de este bar.
listening.meaning: I recommend you try the gazpacho in this bar.
listening.note: New word: el gazpacho = cold tomato soup.

listening.text: Los vecinos nos piden que no hagamos ruido por la noche.
listening.meaning: The neighbours ask us not to make noise at night.
listening.note: New word: el ruido = the noise.

listening.text: Espero que lo paséis muy bien en la boda de vuestros amigos.
listening.meaning: I hope you have a great time at your friends' wedding.

listening.text: Mi hermano dice que está bien, pero yo quiero que vaya al médico.
listening.meaning: My brother says he's fine, but I want him to go to the doctor.
listening.note: Decir que reports with the indicative; querer que asks with the subjunctive.

guide.tip: One person doing both: quiero venir. Two people: quiero que vengas. With decir, ask: a report (indicative) or an order (subjunctive)?

bites.title: One person: infinitive
bites.rule: If the one who wants, hopes or prefers is also the one who acts, use the infinitive: quiero ir, espero aprobar, prefiero cocinar.
bites.example_meaning: I need to rest a little.

bites.title: Someone else: que + subjunctive
bites.rule: When you want, ask, advise, allow or forbid someone ELSE to act: querer / pedir / aconsejar / permitir / prohibir que + subjunctive.
bites.example_meaning: I advise you to leave early.

bites.title: Decir: report or order
bites.rule: Decir que + indicative reports what someone says (dice que viene). Decir que + subjunctive tells someone to do something (me dice que venga).
bites.example: Dice que tiene frío y me dice que cierre la ventana.
bites.example_meaning: She says she's cold and tells me to close the window.

bites.title: Ojalá and ¡Que…!
bites.rule: Ojalá always takes the subjunctive. A bare que + subjunctive is a ready-made wish: ¡Que te mejores! ¡Que aproveche! ¡Que tengas suerte! ¡Que lo pases bien!
bites.example: Ojalá tengas suerte en el examen.
bites.example_meaning: I hope you're lucky in the exam.

sorts.title: Infinitive or que + subjunctive?
sorts.why: If one person does both, use the infinitive. If someone else does the second action, use que + subjunctive.

sorts.title: Report or order?

items.text: Mi padre dice que está cansado.
Mi padre me dice que descanse.

sorts.why: Decir que + indicative passes on information; decir que + subjunctive tells someone to do something.

sorts.title: Which wish?

items.text: Your colleagues sit down to lunch.
A friend has a job interview.

sorts.why: ¡Que aproveche! is for meals, ¡Que te mejores! for illness and ¡Que tengas suerte! for a challenge ahead.

spots.sentence: Quiero que vienes a mi casa.
spots.why: Querer que + a different subject takes the subjunctive: vengas.

spots.sentence: Espero que tienes un buen día.
spots.why: Esperar que + a different subject takes the subjunctive: tengas.

spots.sentence: Mi madre quiere que yo estudiar más.
spots.why: After que comes a conjugated verb in the subjunctive, never an infinitive.
Ojalá always takes the subjunctive: haga.

spots.sentence: El médico me recomienda que duermo más.
Ana dice que esté cansada hoy.
spots.why: Ana is reporting how she feels, so decir que takes the indicative: está.

builds.text: Te pido que cierres la puerta.
builds.meaning: I'm asking you to close the door.
I hope you have lots of luck tomorrow.

builds.text: Prefiero cenar en casa esta noche.
builds.meaning: I'd rather have dinner at home tonight.

builds.text: Me dice que la llame luego.
builds.meaning: She tells me to call her later.
